question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund incurred a business loss of INR 12 crore in FY2024-25 from derivatives (non-speculative). In FY2025-26 the fund earned business income of INR 9 crore from F&O and LTCG of INR 6 crore from listed equities. Under Sections 72 and 74 of the ITA, how can the loss be set off?

answer.text: INR 9 crore set off against F&O business income; remaining INR 3 crore carried forward as business loss (not against capital gains)
INR 12 crore set off against F&O INR 9 crore + LTCG INR 3 crore = zero taxable income
INR 12 crore fully carried forward; no set-off this year
INR 6 crore set off against LTCG only; balance INR 6 crore lapses

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 72 permits a carried-forward non-speculative business loss to be set off only against business or profession income of subsequent years; it cannot be set off against capital gains. Section 74 separately limits set-off of capital losses to capital gains. So INR 9 crore of carried-forward business loss offsets the F&O business income, INR 3 crore is carried forward further, and the INR 6 crore LTCG remains taxable. The Trap: Option B wrongly offsets the carried-forward business loss against LTCG, which Section 72 does not allow. Option C says no set-off is permitted, ignoring the Section 72 rule. Option D inverts the head-matching rule and assumes the balance lapses. Note: Carried-forward business loss under Section 72 can be set off against business income for up to 8 assessment years after the year of loss.
